name: Oxford Quantum Circuits
desc: Builds superconducting quantum computers and sells access via cloud and data-centre installations to businesses, governments and researchers.
markets: UK base with quantum systems installed in partner data centres in New York and Tokyo; enterprise and government users.
rationale: Deep-tech showcase could suit F1 technology partnerships, but small B2B audience and early commercial stage limit fit.

name: Bright Machines
desc: Provides software-defined robotic assembly systems and automation software for electronics and AI-server manufacturing, sold to manufacturers.
markets: Mainly US electronics and AI-hardware manufacturers; backed by Nvidia and Microsoft; no verified detail on wider markets.
rationale: Automation technology story fits F1 engineering themes, but niche B2B buyers make sponsorship value modest.

name: nLIGHT
desc: Designs and manufactures semiconductor and fibre lasers for industrial, microfabrication and defence and directed-energy applications.
markets: Sells to industrial and defence customers in North America, Europe and Asia; manufacturing in the US and Finland.
rationale: B2B component supplier with growing defence focus and little marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Wrench Group
desc: Provides residential heating, cooling, plumbing and electrical repair and replacement services to US homeowners through local brands.
markets: Homeowners in a number of US metropolitan areas only; no international operations or plans known.
rationale: US-only home services roll-up selling through local brands; little reason to buy global F1 exposure.

name: Polar Semiconductor
desc: Operates a 200mm wafer fab in Minnesota making power, sensor and automotive-grade chips under contract for chip companies.
markets: Single fab in Minnesota; long-standing customers include Allegro MicroSystems and Japan's Sanken Electric.
rationale: Contract foundry with few large B2B customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.
changed: Recapitalised in 2024 by US investors with CHIPS Act support; Sanken and Allegro reduced to minority stakes

name: Allegion
desc: Makes locks, door hardware, electronic access control and workforce productivity systems under brands such as Schlage, Von Duprin and CISA.
markets: Mainly the Americas, plus Europe and Asia-Pacific; sells to building owners, contractors, distributors and homeowners.
rationale: Security and smart-access technology could use F1 for B2B hospitality and brand building in the US and Europe.
changed: Spun off from Ingersoll Rand in 2013

name: Western Digital
desc: Designs and makes hard disk drives and storage platforms for cloud data centres, enterprises and consumers.
markets: Sells worldwide to hyperscale cloud providers, PC makers and retail buyers in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global storage brand selling into AI and cloud data centres; F1 data and hospitality could support enterprise sales.
changed: Spun off its flash memory business as Sandisk in 2025

name: Landis+Gyr
desc: Makes smart electricity, gas, water and heat meters plus grid-edge software and services for utilities.
markets: Utilities in over 30 countries, with largest businesses in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Sells to regulated utilities; energy-transition story exists but sponsorship would add little commercial value.

name: AirTrunk
desc: Develops and operates hyperscale data centre campuses leased to large cloud and AI customers across Asia-Pacific.
markets: Campuses in Australia, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong and India; serves hyperscale cloud and AI tenants.
rationale: Infrastructure supplier to a handful of hyperscalers; limited brand need, though APAC B2B hospitality is possible.
changed: Acquired by Blackstone and CPP Investments in 2024

name: Switch
desc: Builds and operates large colocation data centre campuses in the US for cloud, technology and enterprise customers.
markets: Campuses in Nevada, Michigan, Georgia and Texas; customers are US cloud, technology and enterprise firms.
rationale: Las Vegas base gives some local Grand Prix hospitality logic, but a US-only B2B operator gains little.
changed: Taken private by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors in 2022

name: EdgeConneX
desc: Develops, builds and operates edge and hyperscale data centres for cloud providers, content networks and enterprises.
markets: Facilities across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific for hyperscale and cloud tenants.
rationale: Global infrastructure provider, but a small set of hyperscale buyers makes F1 sponsorship of limited use.
changed: Acquired by EQT Infrastructure from Providence Equity Partners

name: Edgecore Digital Infrastructure
desc: Develops and operates large data centre campuses leased to hyperscale cloud and technology customers.
markets: Data centre campuses in the US; no verified operations outside the US.
rationale: Wholesale capacity sold to a few hyperscalers; little need for consumer or broad B2B brand exposure.

name: VEON
desc: Owns mobile telecom and digital services operators such as Kyivstar, Jazz, Banglalink and Beeline in emerging markets.
markets: Operates in Ukraine, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan; Russian business sold in 2023.
rationale: Large consumer telecom brands in South and Central Asia and Ukraine; F1 could support digital services, though markets lack races.
changed: Sold its Russian operations in 2023; headquarters moved to Dubai

name: Vertiv
desc: Supplies power, thermal management, racks and services for data centres, communication networks and industrial sites.
industry: data centre power and cooling equipment
markets: Operates in more than 40 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Fast-growing AI infrastructure supplier; F1 thermal-engineering showcase and B2B hospitality with hyperscale and colocation buyers.
changed: Formerly Emerson Network Power; listed in 2020 through a SPAC merger

name: Wolfspeed
desc: Produces silicon carbide wafers, materials and power semiconductor devices for electric vehicles, energy and industrial power.
markets: Sells to automakers and power electronics firms in North America, Europe and Asia; fabs in North Carolina and New York.
rationale: EV power-electronics supplier could use F1 hybrid technology story, but post-restructuring finances limit sponsorship spend.
changed: Renamed from Cree in 2021; completed Chapter 11 restructuring in 2025

name: Khazna Data Centers
desc: Builds and operates wholesale and AI-focused data centres for hyperscalers, cloud providers, enterprises and government in the UAE.
markets: Largest UAE data centre operator; expansion in Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey and Italy.
rationale: Abu Dhabi AI infrastructure flagship; parent G42 already links to F1, so a Gulf race tie-in has a clear story.
f1: Majority owner G42 is a current Formula 1 partner

name: Serverfarm
desc: Develops and operates colocation, wholesale and build-to-suit data centres for enterprise, cloud and technology customers.
markets: Data centres in North America and Europe; customers are enterprise, cloud and technology firms.
rationale: B2B infrastructure sold to a narrow buyer group; weak case for F1 sponsorship.

name: STACK Infrastructure
desc: Develops and leases wholesale data centre campuses and capacity to hyperscale cloud providers and large enterprises.
markets: Campuses in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific serving hyperscale and large enterprise tenants.
rationale: Global footprint but few, very large customers; F1 adds hospitality value at best.
changed: Sponsor IPI Partners was acquired by Blue Owl in 2024

name: AtlasEdge
desc: Operates edge data centres in European cities offering colocation and interconnection to cloud, content, telecom and enterprise customers.
markets: Data centres in around a dozen European countries; formed as a joint venture of Liberty Global and DigitalBridge.
rationale: Europe-only B2B infrastructure; F1 could offer hospitality but there is no consumer brand need.

name: VSE Corporation
desc: Distributes aircraft parts and provides maintenance, repair and overhaul of engine and airframe components for aviation customers.
markets: Commercial and business aviation customers mainly in North America, with operations and customers abroad.
rationale: Niche aviation aftermarket supplier with B2B customers and little brand marketing; weak F1 fit overall.
changed: Sold its fleet parts segment in 2025 to focus on aviation; headquarters moved to Florida

name: CyrusOne
desc: Owns and operates colocation and hyperscale data centres leased to cloud providers, enterprises and AI workloads.
markets: Over 40 data centres in North America, Europe and Japan for cloud and enterprise tenants.
rationale: Large B2B infrastructure operator; F1 hospitality possible but no clear marketing need.
changed: Taken private by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in 2022

name: CACI International
desc: Provides intelligence, cyber, communications, enterprise IT and mission technology services to US defence and intelligence agencies.
markets: Almost entirely US federal government customers, with a small UK business.
rationale: US government contractor with no commercial brand need or consumer audience; very weak F1 fit.

name: CONMED
desc: Makes surgical devices for orthopaedics, general surgery and gastroenterology, including AirSeal insufflation and arthroscopy products.
markets: Hospitals and surgery centres in the US and over 100 countries worldwide.
rationale: Hospital-focused device maker with no consumer marketing; weak F1 fit despite sports-medicine products.

name: DC BLOX
desc: Builds and operates data centres, fibre networks and subsea cable landing stations in the south-eastern United States.
markets: Customers in the south-eastern US, including Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee and the Carolinas; no international operations.
rationale: US regional infrastructure provider selling only to B2B buyers in one region; weak F1 fit.

name: Ascenty
desc: Builds and operates data centres and connecting fibre networks for cloud providers and enterprises in Latin America.
markets: Data centres in Brazil, Chile and Mexico serving cloud providers and enterprises.
rationale: Latin American B2B infrastructure; Sao Paulo Grand Prix hospitality possible, but no brand need.
parent: Digital Realty (joint venture with Brookfield Infrastructure)
changed: Acquired by Digital Realty in 2018; minority stake later sold to Brookfield Infrastructure

name: Xpansiv
desc: Runs the CBL exchange and registry and data services for carbon credits, renewable energy certificates and other environmental commodities.
markets: Energy companies, corporates and traders in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; origins in Australia.
rationale: Sustainability market infrastructure; F1 net-zero story gives a narrow angle, but B2B audience is small.

name: EcoDataCenter
desc: Builds and operates data centres in Sweden powered by renewable electricity for high-performance computing and cloud customers.
markets: Data centre sites in Sweden serving domestic and international computing customers; no verified sites abroad.
rationale: Swedish B2B infrastructure with a sustainability story; little reason to sponsor F1.

name: Flo Networks
desc: Operates fibre-optic networks and provides connectivity and data services to carriers and businesses, mainly in Mexico.
markets: Mainly Mexico, with cross-border links to the US; no verified operations elsewhere.
rationale: Wholesale fibre operator with business customers; Mexico City Grand Prix hospitality is the only angle.

name: KUBRA
desc: Provides billing, payments, outage communication and customer experience software and services to utilities, insurers and governments.
markets: Utilities and public bodies in the United States and Canada.
rationale: North American utility software vendor with a narrow B2B buyer base; no clear commercial case for F1.
changed: Acquired by Hearst in 2012; recent ownership not verified

name: Lutech
desc: Provides IT services, systems integration, cloud, cybersecurity and digital transformation to Italian businesses and public bodies.
markets: Mainly enterprises and public bodies in Italy; no verified significant international operations.
rationale: Italian IT integrator; Monza and Imola hospitality could serve B2B clients, but national scope limits value.

name: Endava
desc: Provides outsourced software engineering, digital transformation, AI and IT consulting services to large companies in payments, finance, insurance and telecoms.
markets: Clients mainly in North America and Europe; delivery centres in Europe, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Mid-sized B2B services firm; F1 hospitality could help win enterprise clients, but marketing budgets are modest.

name: Meter
desc: Designs, installs and manages wired and wireless enterprise networks for businesses, sold as a subscription service.
markets: Business customers mainly in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Venture-backed US networking start-up; F1 sponsorship would be out of scale for now.

name: Skylo
desc: Provides satellite messaging and data connectivity for standard smartphones, wearables and IoT devices through mobile carriers and device makers.
markets: Service via partners such as Google, Samsung, Verizon and Deutsche Telekom in North America and Europe.
rationale: Consumer-facing satellite SOS technology could suit a connectivity partnership, but the brand sits behind carriers and phones.

name: Cape
desc: Operates a privacy-focused mobile network service for US government, defence and privacy-conscious consumer and business users.
markets: United States customers only, mainly government and defence users plus some consumers.
rationale: Young US-only carrier focused on government and defence users; very weak F1 fit at this stage.

name: CoreSite
desc: Operates colocation data centres and interconnection hubs in major US metro markets for enterprises, cloud providers and networks.
markets: Data centres in about ten US metro markets; customers are enterprises, cloud providers and networks.
rationale: US-only B2B data centre business owned by a tower company; little F1 rationale beyond hospitality.
changed: Acquired by American Tower in 2021

name: Conclusion
desc: Group of specialised IT companies providing software, cloud, data, security and consulting services to Dutch businesses and government.
markets: Mainly enterprises and public bodies in the Netherlands; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Dutch B2B IT group; Dutch Grand Prix hospitality is the only angle, and it is a weak one.

name: MariaDB
desc: Sells enterprise editions, support and cloud services for the MariaDB open-source relational database to businesses.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; open-source user base worldwide.
rationale: Developer-focused database vendor with limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit compared with larger data-platform rivals.
changed: Listed via SPAC on NYSE in 2022; taken private by K1 Investment Management in 2024

name: Hexatronic Group
desc: Makes fibre-optic cables, ducts, connectivity products and installation systems for telecom, data centre and utility network builders.
markets: Operations in Sweden, Germany, the UK, the US and other markets; customers are network builders and operators.
rationale: Fibre infrastructure supplier selling to network builders; weak F1 case beyond occasional B2B hospitality.

name: Zetrix
desc: Develops the Zetrix public blockchain, digital identity and tokenisation services for governments and businesses in Malaysia and China.
markets: Malaysia, with cross-border blockchain links to China; no verified wider international business.
rationale: Government-linked blockchain platform; Asian tech branding possible but weak F1 commercial case.

name: Eclairion
desc: Operates a data centre south of Paris hosting high-performance computing and AI infrastructure for research bodies and companies.
industry: HPC and AI data centre hosting
markets: Customers in France; no verified operations outside France.
rationale: Single French HPC hosting site with a small specialist customer base; no brand need for F1.

name: Axway
desc: Sells API management, managed file transfer and B2B integration software to enterprises, banks and governments.
markets: Thousands of enterprise customers across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise integration software vendor with modest marketing budget; weak to moderate F1 fit.
changed: Listed parent Axway Software renamed 74Software in 2025 after acquiring Sopra Banking Software

name: Systex
desc: Provides software, systems integration, cloud, cybersecurity and financial information systems to banks, brokers, governments and enterprises.
markets: Mainly Taiwan, with operations in mainland China, Hong Kong and South-East Asia.
rationale: Taiwanese IT services group with B2B clients; little reason for global F1 exposure.

name: Upsun
desc: Provides a cloud application platform that lets developers build, deploy and manage web applications across environments.
markets: Developer, agency and software customers in Europe and North America.
rationale: Developer tools vendor with a small marketing budget and technical audience; weak F1 fit.
changed: Formerly Platform.sh; rebranded as Upsun

name: Pivot3
desc: Former maker of hyperconverged storage and computing systems, especially for video surveillance, sold to enterprises and governments.
markets: No longer operating independently; former customers in surveillance and enterprise IT.
rationale: Business no longer exists as an independent company, so there is no sponsor to approach.
changed: Assets acquired by Quantum Corporation in 2021

name: Xtera
desc: Supplied subsea and terrestrial optical transmission systems for long-haul telecom networks to carriers and cable operators.
markets: Former customers were telecom carriers and subsea cable operators; current status not verified.
rationale: Went bankrupt in 2016-17 and current operating status is unclear; no realistic F1 fit.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2016; assets sold out of bankruptcy in 2017

name: Quess Corp
desc: Provides general and IT staffing, workforce management and related business services to enterprises in India and some overseas markets.
markets: Mainly India, with smaller staffing operations in the Middle East and South-East Asia.
rationale: Indian B2B staffing firm with limited marketing culture; weak F1 fit despite rivals Randstad and ManpowerGroup sponsoring.
changed: Demerged into Quess Corp, Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises in 2025

name: LendInvest
desc: Provides buy-to-let mortgages and short-term bridging and development loans to UK property investors through a digital platform.
markets: UK property investors and landlords only; no verified international plans.
rationale: UK-only specialist lender; British Grand Prix hospitality is possible but national scope limits value.
changed: Listed on London's AIM market in 2021

name: TMX Group
desc: Operates the Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture, Montreal Exchange, clearing houses and data businesses such as Trayport.
markets: Mainly Canadian capital markets, with Trayport in Europe and data businesses serving US and global clients.
rationale: Canadian exchange with modest global brand ambitions; Canadian Grand Prix hospitality is the main angle.

name: Brookfield
desc: Manages and invests capital in infrastructure, renewable power, real estate, private equity and credit for institutional and private investors.
markets: Operations and investors across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Global investor whose clients are institutions; F1 hospitality could serve investor relations, but brand need is low.
changed: Brookfield Asset Management moved its headquarters to New York in 2025

name: Victory Capital
desc: Manages mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts through multiple investment franchises for advisers, institutions and individual investors.
markets: Mainly US clients; investment staff in London, Hong Kong and Singapore.
rationale: US asset manager with consumer fund products; F1 fit is weak to moderate, mainly for US hospitality.
changed: Acquired Amundi US in 2025

name: SEGRO
desc: Owns, develops and leases modern warehouses and urban industrial property to logistics, retail and e-commerce tenants.
markets: UK and continental Europe, including France, Germany, Italy, Poland and Spain.
rationale: Industrial landlord serving B2B logistics tenants; little brand value from F1 beyond hospitality.

name: Western Union
desc: Provides cross-border money transfer, payments and foreign exchange services to consumers and businesses through agents, digital apps and online.
markets: Consumers in more than 200 countries and territories, strongest in migrant remittance corridors.
rationale: Global consumer payments brand; F1 audiences in remittance markets and rival payment brands already sponsor teams.
changed: Agreed to acquire Intermex in 2025

name: CBRE Investment Management
desc: Manages real estate, infrastructure and real-asset investments for pension funds, insurers and sovereign wealth funds.
markets: Institutional investors and assets across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Institutional fund manager within CBRE Group; little brand need and only minor hospitality value.

name: CI Financial
desc: Provides mutual funds, asset management and wealth advisory services to Canadian and US investors and advisors.
markets: Canada and the United States; Australian business previously sold.
rationale: Wealth manager targeting affluent clients; Canadian Grand Prix hospitality possible but fit is moderate.
changed: Taken private by a Mubadala Capital-led group in 2025; delisted from TSX and NYSE

name: Cloud Capital
desc: Investment management firm based in Washington, DC; its investment focus and ownership could not be verified.
markets: No verified information on clients, markets or international activity.
rationale: Unverified investment firm with no known consumer brand or marketing activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Propel Finance
desc: Provides asset finance, such as equipment and vehicle leasing and hire purchase, to UK small and medium businesses.
markets: UK small and medium businesses only; no verified international plans.
rationale: UK-only lender to small businesses with no international plans; weak F1 fit beyond British hospitality.

name: Strive
desc: Offers ETFs and asset management and operates a bitcoin treasury strategy as a listed holding company.
markets: US investors and shareholders only; no verified international operations or plans.
rationale: Bitcoin-focused listed company; crypto sponsors exist in F1, but Strive has little consumer marketing need.
changed: Merged with Asset Entities in 2025 to form Nasdaq-listed Strive Inc.; agreed to acquire Semler Scientific

name: TPG
desc: Manages private equity, growth, impact, real estate and credit funds for pension funds and other institutional investors.
markets: Investors and portfolio companies across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Institutional investor with sports investments; F1 hospitality could help fundraising, but brand need is limited.

name: Investcorp
desc: Manages private equity, real estate, credit, infrastructure and other alternative investments for institutional and private wealth clients.
markets: Offices and investments in the Gulf, US, Europe, India and East Asia.
rationale: Gulf-based investor with private-wealth clients; Bahrain and Gulf Grand Prix hospitality give a clear angle.

name: Willis Lease Finance
desc: Leases commercial jet engines and aircraft to airlines and provides engine trading, maintenance and asset management services.
markets: Airline and maintenance customers across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Niche aviation lessor selling to airlines and maintenance firms; weak F1 fit for sponsorship.

name: Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners
desc: Manages funds investing in renewable power, storage, grid and data-centre energy infrastructure for institutional investors.
markets: Projects in the US, UK and Australia; investors are institutions.
rationale: Specialist institutional infrastructure manager with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond investor hospitality.

name: Aukera
desc: Brussels-based investment company focused on energy assets; holdings, clients and ownership could not be verified.
markets: No verified information on markets, holdings or international activity.
rationale: Little-known energy investor with no consumer brand or verified marketing activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Focus Financial Partners
desc: Owns and supports a partnership of independent wealth management firms advising high-net-worth families and individuals.
markets: Mainly the United States, with partner firms in Canada, the UK and Australia.
rationale: Wealth advisers serve affluent clients; hospitality value exists but firms market locally; moderate to weak fit.
changed: Taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2023; delisted from Nasdaq

name: Swan Bitcoin
desc: Provides bitcoin buying, recurring purchases, bitcoin IRAs and private-client services to US individuals and businesses.
markets: Customers in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Crypto platforms sponsor F1, but Swan is a small US-only business; weak to moderate fit.

name: Stem
desc: Provides AI-driven energy storage and solar asset management software and services for commercial, utility and project developer customers.
markets: Mainly the United States, with solar monitoring customers in other countries.
rationale: Clean-energy software vendor under financial strain; little capacity or need for F1 sponsorship spend.
changed: Listed via SPAC in 2021; refocused from hardware to software and services

name: Altruist
desc: Provides custody, brokerage, trading and portfolio management software for independent registered investment advisers and their clients.
markets: Independent financial advisers in the United States only.
rationale: US-only B2B fintech for financial advisers with no international plans; weak F1 fit.

name: Miami International Holdings
desc: Operates options, futures and equities exchanges such as MIAX Options, Pearl and Emerald, plus the Bermuda Stock Exchange.
markets: Mainly US trading firms and brokers; also owns the Bermuda Stock Exchange.
rationale: Exchange operator with B2B customers; Miami Grand Prix hospitality is an angle, but brand need is limited.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2025

name: Virtus Investment Partners
desc: Manages mutual funds, ETFs and institutional accounts through multiple affiliated investment managers and sub-advisers.
markets: Mainly US retail and institutional investors; no verified major international business.
rationale: US asset manager with little consumer marketing and mainly domestic clients; weak F1 fit.

name: DigitalBridge
desc: Invests in and manages digital infrastructure such as data centres, cell towers, fibre and small cells for institutional investors.
markets: Investments in the Americas, Europe and Asia; offices in the US, London and Singapore.
rationale: Institutional investor in data infrastructure; B2B hospitality is the only angle, so F1 fit is weak.
changed: Formerly Colony Capital; SoftBank Group agreed to acquire it (announced around end-2025), completion not confirmed

name: Slate Asset Management
desc: Manages real estate and infrastructure investment funds and listed vehicles such as Slate Grocery REIT for investors.
markets: Assets in Canada, the United States and Europe; institutional and retail investors.
rationale: Mid-sized property investment manager with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond Canadian hospitality.

name: Apex Group
desc: Provides fund administration, depositary, middle-office, banking and ESG services to asset managers and institutional investors.
markets: Offices in dozens of countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global B2B financial services firm; F1 hospitality could support client relations with asset managers.

name: Finnfund
desc: Finnish state-owned development financier investing in companies and projects in developing countries, such as renewable energy and finance.
markets: Investments in Africa, Asia and Latin America from Finland.
rationale: State-owned development financier with no commercial brand to market; F1 sponsorship makes no sense.

name: Acadian Asset Management
desc: Runs quantitative equity and multi-asset investment strategies for pension funds and other institutional investors.
markets: Institutional clients worldwide; offices in Boston, London, Singapore and Sydney.
rationale: Institutional quantitative manager with no consumer brand or marketing culture; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from BrightSphere Investment Group in 2025

name: Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure
desc: Invests in middle-market infrastructure such as power generation, renewables and utilities for institutional investors.
markets: Assets in North America and Europe for institutional investors.
rationale: Institutional infrastructure manager with no brand need or consumer audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Patria Investments
desc: Manages private equity, infrastructure, real estate, credit and public equity funds focused on Latin America for investors.
markets: Mainly Latin America, especially Brazil, with offices in Sao Paulo and other regional cities.
rationale: Latin American asset manager; Sao Paulo and Mexico City Grand Prix hospitality is an angle, but brand need is low.

name: Euroclear
desc: Provides securities settlement, custody and collateral management services to banks, brokers and institutional investors worldwide.
markets: Market participants in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific; depositories in several European countries.
rationale: Pure B2B market infrastructure, politically sensitive over frozen Russian assets; weak F1 fit.

name: Inseego
desc: Makes 5G mobile hotspots, fixed wireless access routers and cloud network management software for carriers and businesses.
markets: Mainly United States mobile operators and enterprises; telematics business sold in 2024.
rationale: Small hardware supplier selling through carriers; little marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Sold its telematics business in 2024

name: StepStone Group
desc: Provides customised private markets investment programmes, funds and advisory services to pension funds, sovereign funds and wealthy investors.
markets: Clients and offices across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Global institutional advisor; F1 hospitality could support client relations, but brand need is limited.

name: Betashares
desc: Issues exchange-traded funds and operates a direct investing platform for Australian retail investors, advisers and institutions.
markets: Australian investors and advisers only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Consumer-facing Australian investment brand; Australian Grand Prix tie-in could reach retail investors.

name: The RMR Group
desc: Manages publicly listed real estate investment trusts and related operating companies in exchange for management fees.
markets: United States real estate assets and investors only.
rationale: US-focused real estate manager with institutional clients and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Beltone
desc: Makes hearing aids and hearing care products sold through independently owned hearing care centres to consumers.
markets: US and Canada through over 1,500 centres, plus more than 40 other countries.
rationale: Consumer health brand targeting older audiences; F1 reach is a moderate to weak fit.
changed: Acquired by GN Store Nord in 2000

name: Global Infrastructure Partners
desc: Invests in and manages energy, transport, water and waste infrastructure assets on behalf of institutional investors.
markets: Infrastructure assets and investors across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Institutional infrastructure investor now within BlackRock; no standalone brand need for F1.
changed: Acquired by BlackRock in 2024

name: Pico
desc: Provides low-latency network infrastructure, market data, managed hosting and Corvil analytics to banks, exchanges and trading firms.
markets: Financial institutions in trading hubs across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Specialist trading technology supplier; F1 speed theme fits, but the audience is a small B2B niche.

name: Cohen & Steers
desc: Manages real estate securities, infrastructure, preferred securities and other real-asset funds for institutions and individual investors.
markets: Mainly US investors, with offices in London, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Singapore.
rationale: Specialist fund manager with limited consumer marketing and mainly US clients; weak F1 fit.

name: Oriente
desc: Builds digital lending and financial services apps for consumers and small businesses in emerging Asian markets.
markets: Emerging markets in South-East Asia; no verified current scale or expansion.
rationale: Small emerging-market fintech with uncertain current status and no global brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Fidelity Investments
desc: Provides mutual funds, brokerage, retirement plans, wealth management and workplace benefits services to individuals and employers.
markets: Mainly US customers, with operations in Canada, Ireland, the UK and India; Fidelity International is separate.
rationale: Major US consumer finance brand; F1's growing US audience and hospitality offer a credible fit.

name: Canoe Financial
desc: Manages mutual funds and investment portfolios sold through financial advisors to Canadian investors.
markets: Canadian investors and advisors only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Canadian fund manager; Canadian Grand Prix hospitality is a narrow angle; weak fit.

name: Econocom
desc: Provides IT equipment leasing, device-as-a-service, workplace and audiovisual infrastructure and digital services to companies and public bodies.
markets: Mainly Europe, especially France, Benelux, Italy and Spain, plus a few other countries.
rationale: European B2B IT services group; hospitality at European races could help, but marketing budgets are modest.

name: Morningstar
desc: Provides investment research, ratings, data and software such as Morningstar Direct and PitchBook to advisers, asset managers and investors.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; also credit ratings via DBRS Morningstar.
rationale: Recognised finance brand with global clients; F1 data storytelling possible, but sponsorship budget unproven.

name: Naver
desc: Runs South Korea's leading search portal plus commerce, Naver Pay, webtoons, maps, cloud and AI services for consumers and businesses.
markets: Mainly South Korea, plus Japan via LY Corporation stake and worldwide readers via Webtoon.
rationale: Strong consumer tech brand with AI ambitions; F1 could support Webtoon and AI global branding.
